title: Ksyusha and Chinchilla
statementMd:
Ksyusha has a pet chinchilla, a tree on $n$ vertices and huge scissors. A tree is a connected graph without cycles. During a boring physics lesson Ksyusha thought about how to entertain her pet.

Chinchillas like to play with *branches*. *A branch* is a tree of $3$ vertices.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d4303a9fbd132e44edb83aa9ef13a54c5c439fc8.png) *The branch* looks like this.

*A cut* is the removal of some (not yet *cut*) edge in the tree. Ksyusha has plenty of free time, so she can afford to make enough *cuts* so that the tree splits into *branches*. In other words, after several (possibly zero) *cuts*, each vertex must belong to **exactly one** *branch*.

Help Ksyusha choose the edges to be *cut* or tell that it is impossible.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$) — number of testcases.

The first line of each testcase contains a single integer $n$ ($2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$) — the number of vertices in the tree.

The next $n - 1$ rows of each testcase contain integers $v_i$ and $u_i$ ($1 \le v_i, u_i \le n$) — the numbers of vertices that the $i$-th edge connects.

It is guaranteed that this set of edges forms a tree. It is also guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all testcases **does not exceed** $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

Print the answer for each testcase.

If the desired way to *cut* the tree does not exist, print $-1$.

Otherwise, print an integer $k$ — the number of edges to be *cut*. In the next line, print $k$ different integers $e_i$ ($1 \le e_i \lt n$) — numbers of the edges to be *cut*. If $k = 0$, print an empty string instead.

If there are several solutions, you can print any.

## Note

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b86684973edb6d8abb366f6686182bd05b57d2c0.png) The first testcase in first test.
statementZhMd:
Ksyusha 有一只宠物绒鼠、一棵有 $n$ 个顶点的树和一把巨大的剪刀。树是一种无环的连通图。在一节无聊的物理课上，Ksyusha 思考着该如何逗她的宠物开心。

绒鼠喜欢玩 *树枝*。*树枝* 是一棵包含 $3$ 个顶点的树。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d4303a9fbd132e44edb83aa9ef13a54c5c439fc8.png) *树枝* 看起来是这样的。

*切割* 是从树中移除一条尚未被*切割*的边。Ksyusha 有充足的空闲时间，因此她可以进行足够多次的*切割*，使这棵树分裂成若干个*树枝*。换句话说，经过若干次（也可以是零次）*切割*后，每个顶点都必须恰好属于一个*树枝*。

请帮助 Ksyusha 选择要*切割*的边，或者判断这是不可能的。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^4$）——测试用例的数量。

每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$）——树中顶点的数量。

接下来的 $n - 1$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $v_i$ 和 $u_i$（$1 \le v_i, u_i \le n$）——第 $i$ 条边所连接的顶点编号。

保证这些边构成一棵树。还保证所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $2 \cdot 10^5$。

## 输出格式

输出每个测试用例的答案。

如果不存在满足要求的*切割*方案，输出 $-1$。

否则，输出一个整数 $k$——需要*切割*的边数。在下一行输出 $k$ 个互不相同的整数 $e_i$（$1 \le e_i \lt n$）——需要*切割*的边的编号。如果 $k = 0$，则输出一个空字符串。

如果有多种方案，输出任意一种即可。

## 说明

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b86684973edb6d8abb366f6686182bd05b57d2c0.png) 第一组测试数据中的第一个测试用例。
